letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.point: Staff finds MISO's August 18 ZGIA submittal deficient and requests more information.
letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.quote: Please be advised that your submittal is deficient and that additional information is necessary to process the filing.

letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.point: Staff asks why a Seasonal Accredited Capacity set by participation type is just and reasonable for a resource that cannot inject beyond its point of interconnection.
letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.quote: Please explain why it is just and reasonable to assign a SAC for a ZG Resource, which cannot inject beyond its point of interconnection, using the currently effective method based on participation type

letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.point: Staff questions treating a 100 MW ZG Interconnection Service resource as equally deliverable as a 100 MW Network Resource Interconnection Service resource.
letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.quote: please explain why it is just and reasonable to consider these two resources as equally deliverable to load.

letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.point: Staff asks how the Transient Tolerance Window will be set per resource, including when it would be shorter than 20 seconds.
letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.quote: Please explain how MISO and the applicable transmission owner will establish the Transient Tolerance Window applicable to each ZG Resource, including the circumstances in which it would require a window shorter than 20 seconds.

letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.point: Staff asks how the ZG Impact Assessment will evaluate injections during the window and the contingencies it will study.
letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.quote: Please explain how MISO will evaluate, in the ZG Impact Assessment, the amount, in MW, of injections during the Transient Tolerance Window

letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.point: MISO has 45 days to respond, and the response amends the filing and sets a new filing date.
letter-er26-3552-miso-deficiency.quote: A response to this letter must be filed with the Secretary of the Commission within 45 days of the date of this letter

filing-20261008-5175.point: The filers say MISO's answer leaves the ZGIA's deficiencies in place.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: MISO’s Answer does not redress the deficiencies of its proposal.

filing-20261008-5175.point: They say the 20-second Transient Tolerance Window is still unjustified.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: MISO did not justify the tariff’s use of a twenty-second Transient Tolerance Window

filing-20261008-5175.point: They say key operating terms belong in the tariff, not the Business Practice Manual.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: It is well-established precedent that key terms must be included in the tariff.

filing-20261008-5175.point: They say termination is MISO's only remedy for injection failures, with nothing at the scale of an injection event.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: The contractual remedy that MISO has proposed functions only as a “last-resort backstop,” offering no consequence other than termination and nothing that operates on the timescale of an injection event.

filing-20261008-5175.point: They say cumulative ZGIA and DPP grid impacts would be resolved in MTEP, which spreads costs to load.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: The Commission should reject the filing as deficient because both MISO’s filing and MISO’s Answer fail to either refute such cumulative impacts or justify their resolution in MTEP, which socializes costs to load more broadly.

filing-20261008-5175.point: They say upgrades needed if a ZG resource never materializes would be socialized through MTEP.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: if a ZG resource does not materialize and thus causes the underlying transmission need to re-emerge, the resulting transmission upgrades that would still be needed to serve the associated load would be broadly socialized via MTEP.

filing-20261008-5175.point: They propose a list of ZGIA data for MISO to publish, starting with quarterly requests by size, technology, location and status.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: Mr. Moaveni instead recommends that the Commission direct MISO to publish: the ZG requests received in each quarterly study period, with megawatt quantity, technology, location, and status;

filing-20261008-5175.point: They say the filing ignores resource adequacy effects of generation dedicated to specific loads, and seek program-wide limits.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: the Filing does not examine how a growing share of generation dedicated to specific loads affects resource adequacy for the rest of the system.

filing-20261008-5175.point: They welcome MISO's hybrid resource clarifications and ask for a broader directive.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: the Commission should issue a broader directive to confirm the other points under discussion in the tariff as well.

filing-20261008-5175.point: They conclude by asking FERC to direct MISO to cure the deficiencies before accepting the filing.
filing-20261008-5175.quote: ask the Commission to use its authority to direct MISO to cure the deficiencies with filing before accepting it.

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS offers conditional support for the ZGIA and does not oppose it.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: OMS cautiously supports the ZGIA proposal

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS treats the ban on injection beyond the substation as a reliability requirement and wants studies before execution.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: That limitation must be treated as a reliability requirement, not merely a contractual condition.

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS objects that MISO left the Transient Tolerance Window definition to its Business Practice Manual.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: MISO has deferred establishing an explicit definition of the appropriate Transient Tolerance Window to the development of its Business Practice Manual.

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS backs keeping the ZGIA limited to generation and load at one substation and voltage level.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: recommends that the Commission accept the common-substation and voltage-level limitation as the appropriate scope of ZGIA.

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS supports the requirement that the generator's full output serve the associated load for at least five years.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: with an expected period of at least five years.

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS says upgrades needed if supporting generation fails to materialize should not automatically fall on existing customers.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: the costs of that incremental need should not automatically shift to existing transmission customers.

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS asks MISO to explain ZGIA treatment across its resource adequacy models, including LOLE, UCAP, SAC and the Planning Resource Auction.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: OMS requests that MISO explain in a compliance filing, subsequent BPM rules, or a workshop how ZGIA resources and associated loads will be represented in

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS wants any later move to injection rights sequenced so it does not bypass the Definitive Planning Process queue.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: must not allow a ZGIA resource to circumvent or obtain an advantage over interconnection customers already participating in the DPP queue.

filing-20260911-5203.point: OMS asks FERC to judge the ZGIA together with MISO's other large-load reforms on a complete record.
filing-20260911-5203.quote: the Commission should evaluate the ZGIA Filing together with other reforms developed during that process only after a complete record is developed

filing-20260908-5341.point: The protesters accept the ZGIA design and object to the missing tariff mechanics.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: Our organizations do not oppose the intended design of MISO’s ZGIA Proposal

filing-20260908-5341.point: They ask FERC to send MISO a deficiency letter or order further compliance in the show cause docket.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: we urge the Commission to direct MISO to address these tariff and procedural defects through either a deficiency letter or direct further compliance via the show cause proceeding.

filing-20260908-5341.point: They want operational penalties for unauthorized injections, citing the E-8 order's concern about control and protection requirements.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: The Commission should require MISO to modify its ZGIA proposal to include robust operational penalties for ZGIA Generating Facilities that make unauthorized injections

filing-20260908-5341.point: They say MISO has not justified the 20-second Transient Tolerance Window.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: MISO has not justified why a maximum period of 20 seconds is either operationally attainable by a generator

filing-20260908-5341.point: They say MISO falls short of the E-8 order's cost transparency requirements.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: MISO has fallen well short of the Order’s clear requirements on transparency.

filing-20260908-5341.point: They ask for a cap on the ZGIA program's size or duration, citing the ERAS and SPP HILLGA precedents.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: To achieve the narrow tailoring required by the Commission’s open access precedents, a program that bypasses the traditional interconnection queue must have some limitation on how large it could get.

filing-20260908-5341.point: They say deferred upgrade costs could reach other customers if supporting generation fails.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: the Proposal does not require adequate financial security, cost-recovery agreements, or true-ups for the cost of deferred transmission upgrades if the ZG Generating Facility fails to materialize, retires early, or becomes permanently unavailable.

filing-20260908-5341.point: They call the five-year commitment an intent, not a firm term, and unsupported by evidence.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: Beyond this bald statement, MISO provides no evidentiary basis for choosing this inadequate formulation and therefore is arbitrary.

filing-20260908-5341.point: They conclude that MISO has the structure for a reasonable co-location program and should cure defects before acceptance.
filing-20260908-5341.quote: Since MISO has the structure for a reasonable co-location program, we urge the Commission to direct MISO to cure the deficiencies with filing before accepting it.

filing-20260908-5329.point: Consumers Energy takes no position on the merits of MISO's proposal.
filing-20260908-5329.quote: Consumers Energy takes no position on whether MISO’s proposal is just and reasonable.

filing-20260908-5329.point: It lists four elements for any acceptance order, from limiting the tariff to jurisdictional services to coordination and transparency for state regulators.
filing-20260908-5329.quote: (1) limit the tariff to Commission-jurisdictional services and practices; (2) preserve state authority over retail loads and retail cost recovery;

filing-20260908-5329.point: It cites the E-8 show cause order's statements that states keep authority over co-located load retail terms and rate design.
filing-20260908-5329.quote: states retain exclusive authority over the specific terms of retail sales and retail rate design, retail cost allocation to co-located load

filing-20260908-5329.point: It asks FERC to carry those statements into the ordering paragraphs, and notes MISO confined the ZGIA to generation and load at the same substation and voltage level.
filing-20260908-5329.quote: MISO’s decision to confine the ZGIA to generation and load at the same substation and voltage level

filing-20260908-5329.point: The conclusion asks FERC to condition approval on clear jurisdictional limits.
filing-20260908-5329.quote: requests that the Commission condition any approval on clear jurisdictional limitations and expressly state that the approved proposal does not supersede, preempt, or displace state jurisdiction over retail loads.

filing-20260903-5021.point: The Southern Regulators back a seven-day extension of the comment deadline, from September 8 to September 15, 2026.
filing-20260903-5021.quote: The PIOs request that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) extend the comment deadline in this proceeding by seven days from September 8, 2026, to September 15, 2026.

filing-20260903-5021.point: They describe the ZGIA as part of MISO's response to the June 18 show cause order, which offered a choice between explaining the tariff and filing amendments.
filing-20260903-5021.quote: The ZGIA proposal is part of MISO’s response to a recent Show Cause Order,

filing-20260903-5021.point: The ZGIA is a novel framework for studying generators that are co-located with and exclusively serve large loads.
filing-20260903-5021.quote: The ZGIA framework is MISO’s novel proposal to study the interconnection of generating facilities that are co-located with

filing-20260903-5021.point: As retail regulators, they cite their interest in the ZGIA's reliability effect in MISO South and its fit with MISO's overall response.
filing-20260903-5021.quote: the Southern Regulators have a substantial interest in understanding how the ZGIA proposal will impact reliability in MISO South and fit into MISO’s holistic Show Cause Order Response.

filing-20260902-5107.point: The Southern Regulators back a seven-day extension of the comment deadline, from September 8 to September 15, 2026.
filing-20260902-5107.quote: The PIOs request that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) extend the comment deadline in this proceeding by seven days from September 8, 2026, to September 15, 2026.

filing-20260902-5107.point: They describe the ZGIA as part of MISO's response to the June 18 show cause order, which offered a choice between explaining the tariff and filing amendments.
filing-20260902-5107.quote: The ZGIA proposal is part of MISO’s response to a recent Show Cause Order,

filing-20260902-5107.point: The ZGIA is a novel framework for studying generators that are co-located with and exclusively serve large loads.
filing-20260902-5107.quote: The ZGIA framework is MISO’s novel proposal to study the interconnection of generating facilities that are co-located with

filing-20260902-5107.point: As retail regulators, they cite their interest in the ZGIA's reliability effect in MISO South and its fit with MISO's overall response.
filing-20260902-5107.quote: the Southern Regulators have a substantial interest in understanding how the ZGIA proposal will impact reliability in MISO South and fit into MISO’s holistic Show Cause Order Response.

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: MISO says the ZGIA gives expedited review to generation with little transmission impact because it serves load at the same substation.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: The ZGIA proposal will help streamline the MISO generator interconnection process by providing expedited review of the addition of ZG Resources that have little or no impact on the Transmission System because they are limited to serving load at the same substation and voltage level.

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: MISO requests an October 18, 2026 effective date.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: MISO requests that the Tariff revisions submitted herewith be made effective October 18, 2026

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: The filing is partial: it is the first in a series and does not cover all E-8 issues.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: MISO notes that this filing is not intended to address all issues raised in the Show Cause Order.

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: MISO excludes electrically proximate load from the ZGIA and defers it to the LARS process.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: Accordingly, this filing is limited to addressing generation and load at the same substation and does not attempt to resolve the separate issues presented by generation serving electrically proximate large load.

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: The generator cannot inject past the substation, and load and generation are not netted for transmission service or settlement.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: the new generator with ZGIA Interconnection Service cannot inject past the interconnecting substation, and netting of the load and generation for transmission service or market settlement purposes is not allowed

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: Neither the ZGIA nor LARS creates new transmission services or addresses flexible large loads.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: neither the ZGIA construct nor LARS proposal include new transmission service products specific to serving co-located or proximate load or address flexible large loads willing to limit transmission service.

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: MISO expects to file LARS by November 16, 2026, and has not proposed a Large Load definition here.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: MISO will continue to develop the LARS process through the LLWG and expects to submit the LARS filing by November 16, 2026, or earlier, if feasible.

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: A request that meets the criteria gets a 90-day accelerated study.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: If all of these criteria are met, the ZG Interconnection study process affords a 90-day accelerated study process leading to a ZGIA that memorializes the proposed configuration and limited injection.

filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.point: MISO requires only an intent to use the full output for at least five years, not a firm commitment.
filing-er26-3552-miso-zgia.quote: MISO therefore only requires that the agreement specify an intent to use the full output of the Generating Facility for at least five years rather than a firm commitment.
